plan_a_advantages: More frequent running sessions (more days running)
Potentially lower initial fatigue due to the emphasis on easy runs
plan_b_advantages: Includes tempo and aerobic sessions for speed development
Features a dedicated long run for endurance adaptation
More varied workout types to prevent boredom and promote holistic fitness
reasoning: Plan B is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. While Plan A focuses heavily on easy runs, it lacks any structured intensity work, which is crucial for improving speed. Plan B incorporates a tempo run and a longer, controlled effort, directly addressing the goal of increasing sustainable threshold strength – a key component of faster trail running. Furthermore, the inclusion of a dedicated long run is more beneficial than the extended easy run in Plan A, as it allows for adaptation to the demands of trail running distances. Plan A’s repetitive easy runs could lead to plateaus, whereas Plan B provides a more varied and stimulating training stimulus.
